digest.component_or_area: core reconciler dispatcher — capability-guarded outbound mutation
propositions: Four dispatch call sites use static `cast()` to access opt-in capability members (`add_comment`, `set_relationship`) without runtime `isinstance` guards, unlike equivalent code in `fetcher.py` that uses `hasattr`.

When a transport lacks an optional capability, an `AttributeError` at those four sites is silently swallowed by a broad `except Exception` handler, conflating 'designed skip' with 'real failure' and preventing alerting.
Capability-absent mutations are never applied but the pass reports success, creating a latent defect that becomes a live bug once a second backend (Data Center) legitimately omits those capabilities.
`_call_with_retry` (75 LOC) must relocate from `dispatch_one.py` to `dispatch_apply_phases.py` to stay under the 800-LOC module ceiling after adding runtime guards.
Runtime guards use `isinstance(client, SupportsComments|SupportsLinks)` with member-fallback to handle Python 3.11–3.12 compatibility differences in `@runtime_checkable` Protocol resolution.

Capability-absent skips are logged as INFO, recorded on the EXISTING `bridge_alerts` channel with distinct kinds (`outbound-comment-capability-absent`, `outbound-links-capability-absent`), and do NOT trip failure detectors.
